name: Is it better to frame a basement with wood or metal studs?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to frame a basement with wood or metal studs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wood studs remain the traditional standard because they are easy to modify, support heavy shelving or wall-mounted TVs, and accept standard fasteners. However, wood expands and contracts with humidity changes and can warp or rot if exposed to water. Steel framing is completely impervious to moisture, fire-resistant, and stays perfectly straight over time. The tradeoff is that metal studs cost more, require specialized screws, and need extra wood blocking if you plan to hang heavy cabinetry or heavy mirrors later. Your basement moisture levels and wall-mounting plans dictate the best choice.
acceptedAnswer.description: Wood is sturdy, easy to cut, and holds heavy mounts well, while steel studs never warp, rot, or burn. Choose steel if moisture risk is high and wood for easier hanging support.
